references.text: The sin offering goat is required as part of the monthly and festival sacrifices, as first established in the laws concerning new moon offerings.
The same wording regarding one male goat for a sin offering is used repeatedly throughout the sacrificial laws for the Feast of Tabernacles.
Identical wording about the sin offering goat in addition to the daily burnt offering with its accompanying grain and drink offerings.
A parallel passage describing the sin offering and the daily burnt offering on another day of the Feast of Tabernacles.
The repeated pattern of a sin offering goat in addition to the continual burnt offering throughout the entire festival.
The same structure of sin offering and daily burnt offering that characterizes all the days of the Feast of Tabernacles.
The preceding day of the Feast of Tabernacles with identical wording about the sin offering and the daily offering.
The daily burnt offering (tamid) mentioned here was originally commanded in these verses.
The basis for the continual burnt offering (olat hatamid) that was to be offered morning and evening.
